react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on galactose metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this differential metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct activity all rank the galactose / galactosemia pathway as the top or near-top finding (FDR 2.83 × 10⁻¹¹ in RaMP; p = 3.25 × 10⁻⁷ in MetaboAnalystR; rank 4 in mummichog at p = 9.16 × 10⁻³), with four shared driver metabolites: galactinol (α-D-galactosyl-(1→3)-1D-myo-inositol, KEGG:C01235), sucrose (KEGG:C00089), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116). A fifth input metabolite, 8(S)-HPETE (KEGG:C14823), tracks onto the arachidonic acid metabolism network via the mummichog empirical network (rank 6, p = 0.022), consistent with the presence of multiple HPETE positional isomers in that module. D-glucose and dopamine appear in the broader metabolic network but do not independently reach significance in any single pathway, reflecting their pleiotropic roles across many pathways. The cross-paradigm consensus is robust: Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00052 / SMPDB:SMP00043 / SMPDB:SMP00182) is the primary affected pathway, with the four-carbon sugar alcohol myo-inositol serving as a structural bridge between the galactose and glycerophospholipid networks. Dopamine elevates the GPCR downstream signalling and MECP2/Rett syndrome pathways in RaMP ORA, suggesting a secondary central-nervous system signal that warrants further validation. Glycerol additionally anchors the glycerophospholipid biosynthetic pathway (WP:WP2533, rank 11 RaMP) and glycerophospholipid metabolism (rank 5 mummichog). The strong fold-enrichment values (>1000 in RaMP) and tight overlap in the MetaboAnalystR KEGG annotation (4 of 4 possible input metabolites hitting the 27-member pathway) indicate a high-confidence metabolic re-wiring centred on galactose utilisation, with myo-inositol as the key signalling hub connecting carbohydrate and lipid arms of the affected network.

Four metabolites drive this enrichment in every paradigm: galactinol (KEGG:C01235), sucrose (KEGG:C00089), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116). Each of these four maps directly into the 27-member KEGG Galactose Metabolism roster and the 31-member SMPDB Galactose Metabolism roster, confirming structural pathway membership. react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis paradigms converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant biological signal in the differential metabolite set. RaMP multi-DB ORA (SMPDB, KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways) ranks Galactose Metabolism as the top hit across three namespaces: SMPDB:SMP00043 (FDR 2.83 × 10⁻¹¹, p = 4.43 × 10⁻¹³), KEGG:map00052 (FDR 2.83 × 10⁻¹¹), and KEGG:hsa00052 (MetaboAnalystR PSEA, p = 3.25 × 10⁻⁷). The mummichog empirical-compound network independently returns MUMM:galactose_metabolism at rank 4 (p = 8.32 × 10⁻³), with a 10-compound overlap against the 11-member KEGG module. Four metabolites drive this enrichment in every paradigm: galactinol (KEGG:C01235), sucrose (KEGG:C00089), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116). Each of these four maps directly into the 27-member KEGG Galactose Metabolism roster and the 31-member SMPDB Galactose Metabolism roster, confirming structural pathway membership. The remaining three input compounds — 8(S)-HPETE (KEGG:C14823), dopamine (KEGG:C03758), and D-glucose (KEGG:C00221) — are not driver metabolites of this pathway; dopamine appears only in secondary GPCR-related Reactome hits and D-glucose is broadly distributed across several mummichog carbohydrate modules. A secondary signal emerges from mummichog alone: MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism (p = 0.021), consistent with the lipid-oxidative context of the remaining input set.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis paradigms converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant biological signal in the differential metabolite set. RaMP multi-DB ORA (SMPDB, KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways) ranks Galactose Metabolism as the top hit across three namespaces: SMPDB:SMP00043 (FDR 2.83 × 10⁻¹¹, p = 4.43 × 10⁻¹³), KEGG:map00052 (FDR 2.83 × 10⁻¹¹), and KEGG:hsa00052 (MetaboAnalystR PSEA, p = 3.25 × 10⁻⁷). The mummichog empirical-compound network independently returns MUMM:galactose_metabolism at rank 4 (p = 8.32 × 10⁻³), with a 10-compound overlap against the 11-member KEGG module. Four metabolites drive this enrichment in every paradigm: galactinol (KEGG:C01235), sucrose (KEGG:C00089), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116). Each of these four maps directly into the 27-member KEGG Galactose Metabolism roster and the 31-member SMPDB Galactose Metabolism roster, confirming structural pathway membership. The remaining three input compounds — 8(S)-HPETE (KEGG:C14823), dopamine (KEGG:C03758), and D-glucose (KEGG:C00221) — are not driver metabolites of this pathway; dopamine appears only in secondary GPCR-related Reactome hits and D-glucose is broadly distributed across several mummichog carbohydrate modules. A secondary signal emerges from mummichog alone: MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism (p = 0.021), consistent with the lipid-oxidative context of the remaining input set.

use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead
